arxiv-2205-09935.title: Quantitative Analysis of Community Evolution in Developer Social Networks Around Open Source Software Projects CCS: Software and its engineering Programming teams CCS: Software and its engineering Open source model CCS: General and reference Metrics
arxiv-2205-09935.creator: Liang Wang, Ying Li, Jierui Zhang, Xianping Tao
arxiv-2205-09935.description: Abstract . Understanding the evolution of communities in developer social networks (DSNs) around open source software (OSS) projects can provide valuable insights about the socio-technical process of OSS development. Existing studies show the evolutionary behaviors of social communities can effectively be described using patterns including split, shrink, merge, expand, emerge, and extinct.

arxiv-2211-03754.title: A Stochastic Model for Estimating the Number of Offenders and Targets on Snapchat Platform
arxiv-2211-03754.creator: Vasyl Pihur
arxiv-2211-03754.description: Abstract Snapchat, like many other social platforms, provides mechanisms for its users to report content and private/public interactions that violate their sense of safety and decency. From our experience and common sense, we can safely assume that not everybody makes an effort to report, leaving potentially a large number of offending users and content unnoticed.

arxiv-2308-09517.title: Transitivity-Preserving Graph Representation Learning for Bridging Local Connectivity and Role-based Similarity
arxiv-2308-09517.creator: Van Thuy Hoang, O-Joun LeeDepartment of Artificial Intelligence, The Catholic University of KoreaBucheon-si, Gyeonggi-do 14662, Republic of Korea {hoangvanthuy90,ojlee}@catholic.ac.kr
arxiv-2308-09517.description: Abstract Graph representation learning (GRL) methods, such as graph neural networks and graph transformer models, have been successfully used to analyze graph-structured data, mainly focusing on node classification and link prediction tasks. However, the existing studies mostly only consider local connectivity while ignoring long-range connectivity and the roles of nodes.

arxiv-2310-15502.title: Algebraic combinatorial optimization on the degree of determinants of noncommutative symbolic matrices
arxiv-2310-15502.creator: Hiroshi HIRAI, Yuni IWAMASA, Taihei OKI, Tasuku SOMA
arxiv-2310-15502.description: Abstract We address the computation of the degrees of minors of a noncommutative symbolic matrix of form A ⁡ [ c ] := ∑ k = 1 m A k ​ t c k ​ x k , A[c]:=\sum_{k=1}^{m}A_{k}t^{c_{k}}x_{k}, where A k A_{k} are matrices over a field 𝕂 \mathbb{K} , x i x_{i} are noncommutative variables, c k c_{k}

arxiv-2407-12698.title: Paramagnetic limit of spin-triplet superconductors
arxiv-2407-12698.creator: Thomas Bernat, Julia S. Meyer, Manuel Houzet
arxiv-2407-12698.description: Abstract We study the phase diagram of spin-triplet superconductors, considering the effect of the external magnetic field on the electrons’ spins. For a given symmetry of the order parameter and a generic orientation of the field, we find that the paramagnetic limit for superconductivity diverges at low temperatures.

arxiv-2410-12496.title: Finding Logic Bugs in Spatial Database Engines via Affine Equivalent Inputs
arxiv-2410-12496.creator: Wenjing Deng, Qiuyang Mang, Chengyu Zhang, Manuel Rigger
arxiv-2410-12496.description: Abstract .\par Spatial Database Management Systems ( SDBMS s) aim to store, manipulate, and retrieve spatial data . SDBMS s are employed in various modern applications, such as geographic information systems, computer-aided design tools, and location-based services. However, the presence of logic bugs in SDBMS s can lead to incorrect results, substantially undermining the reliability of these applications.

arxiv-2412-07430.title: Knowledge Graph Guided Evaluation of Abstention Techniques
arxiv-2412-07430.creator: Kinshuk Vasisht, Navreet Kaur, Danish Pruthi
arxiv-2412-07430.description: Abstract To deploy language models safely, it is crucial that they abstain from responding to inappropriate requests. Several prior studies test the safety promises of models based on their effectiveness in blocking malicious requests. In this work, we focus on evaluating the underlying techniques that cause models to abstain.

arxiv-2505-18736.title: Rethinking Direct Preference Optimization in Diffusion Models
arxiv-2505-18736.creator: Junyong Kang, Seohyun Lim, Kyungjune Baek, Hyunjung Shim†
arxiv-2505-18736.description: Abstract Aligning text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models with human preferences has emerged as a critical research challenge. While recent advances in this area have extended preference optimization techniques from large language models (LLMs) to the diffusion setting, they often struggle with limited exploration. In this work, we propose a novel and orthogonal approach to enhancing diffusion-based preference optimization.

arxiv-2508-09106.title: Smart Residential Community Simulator for Developing and Benchmarking Energy Management Systems
arxiv-2508-09106.creator: Ninad Gaikwad, and Anamika Dubey
arxiv-2508-09106.description: Abstract Home Energy Management Systems (HEMS) are being actively developed for both individual houses and communities to support demand response in on-grid operation, and ensure resilience during off-grid scenarios. However, most simulators used for closed-loop HEMS testing are tailored to a specific distributed energy resource (DER) configuration with a fixed number of houses, limiting flexibility and scalability.

arxiv-2509-00801.title: Adaptation of Parameters in Heterogeneous Multi-agent Systems
arxiv-2509-00801.creator: Hyungbo Shim, Jin Gyu Lee, and Brian D. O. Anderson
arxiv-2509-00801.description: Abstract This paper proposes an adaptation mechanism for heterogeneous multi-agent systems to align the agents’ internal parameters, based on enforced consensus through strong couplings. Unlike homogeneous systems, where exact consensus is attainable, the heterogeneity in node dynamics precludes perfect synchronization.

pmc-11609452.title: Outcomes of ophthalmology telemedicine in a large health care system beyond initial pandemic crisis☆
pmc-11609452.creator: Elaine I. Wu, Mary Reed, Bradley Frueh, Weilu Wu, H. Jane Kim
pmc-11609452.description: PurposeTo compare the outcome of telemedicine versus in-person visit in a large health care system.DesignRetrospective cohort study.Methods174,245 patients with a telemedicine or in-person visit from September 2020 to June 2021 in the Kaiser Permanente Northern California Health Care System were included.

pmc-12409905.title: A survival prediction model for biliary tract cancer based on least absolute shrinkage and selection operator–cox regression
pmc-12409905.creator: Shanshan Fan, Kexin Zhao, Ziwei Liang, Yang Ge
pmc-12409905.description: BackgroundBiliary tract cancer (BTC) is a digestive tract tumor with low incidence, high malignancy, and short survival times. Abnormal lipid metabolism may be related to the occurrence and development of tumors; therefore, we constructed a survival prediction model for patients with BTC using clinical data that included lipid indicators rarely considered in previous studies.

pmc-12710289.title: Clinical Practice Guideline for Stroke Rehabilitation in Korea—Part 2: Rehabilitation for Motor and Sensory Function (2024)
pmc-12710289.creator: Hyun Haeng Lee, Yong Wook Kim, Hyoung Seop Kim, Seung Nam Yang, Sun Im, Woo-Kyoung Yoo, Joon-Ho Shin, Min-Kyun Oh, Won-Seok Kim, Da-Sol Kim, Won Kee Chang, Seyoung Shin, Sekwang Lee, Doo Young Kim, Sung-Hwa Ko, Yeo Jun Yun, Yookyung Lee, Miyoung Choi, Suk Hoon Ohn, KSNR Stroke CPG Writing Group
pmc-12710289.description: This clinical practice guideline (CPG) is the second part of the fourth edition of the Korean Stroke Rehabilitation Guidelines, following the first part published in 2023. While, the first part addressed rehabilitation for motor function, while this second part focuses on both motor and sensory rehabilitation.

pmc-12742057.title: Clinical decision-making in neonatal gastrointestinal surgical emergencies: comparison between ChatGPT and human clinicians
pmc-12742057.creator: Seyoon Kim, Dongho Choi, Joonhyuk Son
pmc-12742057.description: BackgroundNeonatal gastrointestinal surgical emergencies (NGSEs) require rapid decisions to prevent morbidity and mortality. This study assessed the potential use of ChatGPT in supporting clinical decision-making for NGSEs.MethodsThe challenging NGSE cases (ileal atresia, midgut volvulus, Hirschsprung disease, meconium ileus, and pseudo-obstruction) were converted into structured short-answer questions including histories and radiologic images.

pmc-12787245.title: Evolution of the Metallographic Structure of Additively Manufactured Ti-6Al-4V and Ti-6Al-7Nb Titanium Alloys
pmc-12787245.creator: Dorota Laskowska, Błażej Bałasz, Łukasz Żurawski
pmc-12787245.description: The aim of this study was to evaluate structural changes and their impact on the functional properties of Ti-6Al-4V and Ti-6Al-7Nb titanium alloys produced by L-PBF. In the as-built condition, these alloys, despite high strength due to the presence of metastable α’ martensite, exhibit limited ductility.

pmc-13244457.title: Light-Driven Proton-Coupled Two-Electron Ligand Reduction Causes the Rearrangement of the Coordination Sphere in Cu(I) 4H‑Imidazolato Complexes
pmc-13244457.creator: Luise Thomisch, Louis Blechschmidt, Niklas Klosterhalfen, Phil Köhler, Helmar Görls, Jens H. Tran, Julian Plitzko, Benjamin Dietzek-Ivanšić, Carolin Müller, Martin Schulz
pmc-13244457.description: The direct conversion of solar light into chemical energy, inspired by natural photosynthesis, presents a promising strategy for energy storage and chemical transformation. We investigate this approach using photoactive Cu­(I) complexes with the functional 4H-imidazolato ligand for storage of multiple photoredox equivalents.

pmc-13292689.title: Pediatric lichen sclerosus: a self-limited disease? A long-term follow-up case series؆

pmc-13401030.title: Soil heavy metals in a typical coal mining cluster of Northern China: Pollution, source apportionment, and eco-health risks
pmc-13401030.creator: Dandan Du, Lijing Fang, Shuyu Yu, Yanying Bai, Yusheng Hao, Hao Li
pmc-13401030.description: SummaryCoal mining activities can alter soil heavy-metal accumulation and risk patterns. To identify pollution characteristics, sources, and ecological and health risks, 88 surface soil samples from Tongchuan Town, Ordos City, were analyzed using enrichment factor, potential ecological risk index, positive matrix factorization, soil physicochemical analysis, and Monte Carlo-based health risk assessment.
